title: Lando Norris reveals "painful" McLaren deficit after Bahrain GP
extract: Lando Norris says McLaren's straightline-speed deficit is costing almost two-tenths per lap after a difficult wet Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari’s chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
extract: McLaren and Ferrari committed to slick tyres at the restart in Sepang, a gamble that left both teams fighting back after the track stayed wetter than expected.

title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
extract: The FIA explained how a software bug affecting power deployment at very low speeds caused multiple cars to lose throttle response during the formation lap, forcing an emergency update.

title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Verstappen wins chaotic race from Antonelli as Russell retires late on
extract: Max Verstappen claimed his first 2026 victory at a chaotic Sepang race after rain, software problems and tyre strategy turned the relocated Bahrain Grand Prix into a technical and tactical mess.

title: How the Bahrain GP in Malaysia exposed Red Bull’s hidden resurgence
extract: Autosport analyses how Red Bull’s improved pace at Sepang revealed a genuine late-season resurgence despite Ferrari and McLaren’s wet-weather strategy gamble.

title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Verstappen dominates for first pole of 2026 from Hamilton
extract: Max Verstappen took his first pole of the 2026 season at Sepang, with Lewis Hamilton joining him on the front row for Ferrari.

title: Fulcrum Echo promises AI text in the style of any writer, so I tested it
extract: The Register tests Fulcrum Echo, an AI writing system designed to reproduce the style of a chosen writer, examining what it actually produces.

title: Revive Raskin's 3 laws of software with humane work that considers a dev's duty of care
extract: A look at software-development principles inspired by Jef Raskin and how a more humane approach can change the relationship between developers, users and their work.

title: Spies, prime ministers, and balls: the BBC Domesday project @ 40
extract: The Register revisits the BBC Domesday project four decades on, including the people behind the original multimedia system and those preserving it today.

title: Clever database, but can it run Doom?
extract: A deliberately unusual database experiment asks whether the system can be pushed far enough to run the classic Doom engine, blending database internals with retro computing.

title: Anthropic's super bug-hunting model Mythos is hardcore good at math, as latest vuln under attack shows
extract: The Register examines Anthropic’s Mythos security model and its ability to reason about vulnerabilities as a newly exploited flaw provides a real-world test.

title: Kagi ends Orion development for Linux and Windows and open-sources both platforms
extract: Kagi is ending Orion browser development for Linux and Windows while releasing the source code for those platforms, opening the door to community continuation.

title: Retro Recap: All The Classic Gaming News From The Past Week (October 4th 2026)
extract: Time Extension’s latest retro roundup covers new preservation, homebrew, restoration and classic-hardware stories, including several current fan projects.

title: Donkey Kong '94's Game Boy Color fan remaster reaches playable beta
extract: A long-running ROM-hacking project has produced a start-to-finish beta of Donkey Kong DX, bringing the Game Boy classic to a fully colourised presentation.

title: Mega Splatterhouse Mega Drive fan port is nearing feature completion
extract: Monster Bath Games says its Mega Drive/Genesis port of Splatterhouse is down to its final level before a cleanup pass covering palettes, audio and enemy AI.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Master System project gets a fresh development update
extract: The Master System conversion remains in development, with the creator confirming continued work and a demo potentially coming soon.

title: Daytona USA gets an unofficial PC port
extract: A homebrew developer has created a PC version of the 1994 arcade racer rather than relying on conventional emulation, with the project hosted on GitHub.

title: House of the Dead is being resurrected in arcades using VR
extract: Sega Amusements has teased a new House of the Dead arcade game, with reporting indicating that the new entry will use VR technology.

title: Anbernic RG DS Plus brings a new dual-screen route to Nintendo DS classics
extract: A hands-on review examines Anbernic’s RG DS Plus, a dual-screen emulation handheld designed to make Nintendo DS software more practical on modern hardware.

title: Longines expands Spirit watch collection
extract: Longines expanded the Spirit collection with four new pilot watches using COSC-certified movements, including two flyback chronographs.

title: Casio leaked details of new automatic watch series
extract: New details about Casio’s CMK-100 automatic series point to titanium construction and a mechanical Miyota movement.

title: Corum releases three ceramic Admiral watch models
extract: Corum expanded its Admiral collection with three 39mm ceramic models featuring integrated bracelets and movements developed with Concepto.

title: L. Leroy releases limited VOX Temporis with rotating dial
extract: L. Leroy introduced the VOX Temporis, a 15-piece limited watch with a rotating dial and hand-wound L601SQR movement.

title: Parmigiani Fleurier releases three limited-edition platinum watches
extract: Parmigiani Fleurier introduced three limited-edition 950 platinum watches, including a GMT Rattrapante, Minute Rattrapante and Chronographe Mystérieux.

title: Operation Vienna
extract: Michael Ridpath’s new post-war mystery arrives on October 5, following a murder investigation through Vienna in 1931 against a backdrop of political and financial instability.

title: The Spy Hiding in Plain Sight
extract: A new feature highlights Katherine Reay’s historical mystery The Undercover Bookshop, set in the English Cotswolds in 1950 and built around a woman whose past refuses to stay hidden.

title: Book Deals: Week of October 5, 2026
extract: Publishers Weekly reports new publishing deals including a two-book thriller series from Chris Hanson and several other forthcoming projects.

title: Mindless Mind
extract: Youngwoo Jeon’s new science-fiction novel imagines a humanoid consciousness engineered using a Buddhist model of mind rather than a conventional language model.

title: Avengers: Endgame surpasses Avatar to reclaim all-time box office record
extract: Avengers: Endgame has reclaimed the worldwide box-office record after the Encore reissue pushed its lifetime gross above Avatar.

title: WeeklyTrek wraps up Strange New Worlds season four
extract: TrekCore’s latest WeeklyTrek episode reviews the Strange New Worlds fourth-season finale and discusses new Star Trek developments across television and the wider franchise.

title: Star Trek creator’s son says the franchise is ready for new stories
extract: Rod Roddenberry discusses the future of Star Trek after six decades, arguing that the franchise can move forward while retaining its optimistic view of technology and society.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day passes $950 million domestically
extract: MarvelBlog reports that Spider-Man: Brand New Day has crossed $950 million at the domestic box office, surpassing the previous Star Wars benchmark.

title: James Gunn is already writing his next film after Superman sequel
extract: James Gunn is already working on his next film while awaiting an assembly cut of Man of Tomorrow, offering an early look at his continuing DC plans.

title: Inside the ILM Art Department: The End of Oak Street
extract: ILM’s art department has published a look inside its creative process, with artists from multiple studios sharing work and insights from 2026’s The End of Oak Street.

title: Dave Grohl joins AC/DC for Highway To Hell on final Power Up tour night
extract: Dave Grohl joined AC/DC on guitar and backing vocals for Highway To Hell at the final night of the band’s Power Up tour in New Jersey.
